justice: The street allocates most visible space to wide motor-vehicle lanes, while no clear pedestrian sidewalk or dedicated walking zone is visible, indicating an uneven distribution of street space for all road users.

A landscaped median and side planting strips are present, but there are no visible curb ramps, tactile paving, marked crossings, or bus stop facilities, so accessibility appears limited for users not traveling by car.

The road markings are clear for drivers, yet the absence of visible pedestrian infrastructure and any dedicated non-motorized lane suggests the street serves motorists more fairly than walkers or other non-driving users.
safety: The carriageway is wide and straight with clear centerlines and lane markings, which supports predictable vehicle movement and good forward visibility.

Streetlights are installed along the corridor, which likely improves nighttime driving safety, although their effectiveness for any pedestrian area cannot be confirmed because no sidewalk is clearly visible.

A parked black car on the side access lane/shoulder introduces a potential conflict point, and there are no visible crosswalks, refuge islands, or traffic-calming elements to protect people crossing or walking near the road edge.
